unrecordedQuestions: Where should the "recently viewed" list live — per-browser or per-account? My recommendation: store it client-side in the browser's localStorage (per-device, no backend work, instantly fast). The trade-off is it won't follow a person across devices or browsers, and clearing site data wipes it. Given "keep it simple and fast, a convenience not a feature," I'd lean localStorage — but if you'd rather it follow the user across devices, we'd persist it server-side against their account. Which do you want? (offered choices: Client-side (localStorage, per-browser) — simplest & fastest; Server-side (per-account, follows the user across devices)) (its recommendation: Client-side (localStorage, per-browser))

Good — localStorage per origin, no backend. Next: how should the list behave when someone reopens a doc they've already viewed? My recommendation: dedupe by document and move-to-front, so the strip is always five *distinct* docs ordered most-recent-first (reopening doc A just bumps A to the front rather than adding a second A card). The alternative is a raw chronological log that can show the same doc multiple times. I'd go with dedupe + move-to-front. Agree? (offered choices: Dedupe by doc, move-to-front (5 distinct, most-recent-first); Raw log (may repeat the same doc)) (its recommendation: Dedupe by doc, move-to-front (5 distinct, most-recent-first))

Dedupe by doc, move-to-front — locked in. Next, a robustness question: what happens when a remembered doc has since been deleted, moved, or renamed on the site? My recommendation: keep it lazy and simple — store the doc's URL/id plus a title snapshot, and if a click lands on a doc that no longer resolves, let the site's normal 404/not-found handling take over (we don't proactively validate the strip). We can also drop an entry from the strip if we know at render time it's gone, but I wouldn't add extra lookups just for this. Given "keep it simple," I'd go lazy: no proactive validation, rely on normal not-found handling. Agree? (offered choices: Lazy — no proactive validation, rely on normal 404/not-found on click; Proactively validate/prune stale entries before rendering) (its recommendation: Lazy — no proactive validation, rely on normal 404/not-found on click)
